context: Algebra: associative internally closed operation with two-sided identity

formulations.mathematical_scope_note: The existence of e makes M nonempty. No commutativity or inverses are required; the operation is internally closed by its signature.
formulations.text: A monoid is a pair (M,⋆) consisting of a set M and an operation ⋆:M×M→M for which (a⋆b)⋆c=a⋆(b⋆c) for all a,b,c∈M and some e∈M satisfies e⋆a=a=a⋆e for every a∈M.

context: Two-input operation between potentially distinct sets

formulations.mathematical_scope_note: General codomain U need not equal either input set. Do not silently infer closure on a particular carrier.
formulations.text: For sets S,T,U, a binary operation with input sets S and T and values in U is a function ⋆:S×T→U, assigning exactly one output in U to each ordered pair (s,t)∈S×T.

context: Internal binary operation closed on a set

formulations.mathematical_scope_note: Closure is part of the mapping type; this is the correct algebraic operation convention for groups and monoids.
formulations.text: An internal binary operation on a set S is a function ⋆:S×S→S, assigning to each pair (a,b)∈S×S a uniquely determined element a⋆b∈S.

context: Typed relation with explicit domain and codomain

formulations.mathematical_scope_note: Under this convention source and target sets are data of the relation, not merely metadata; different triples can share the same relation graph R.
formulations.text: A binary relation from a set S to a set T may be defined as an ordered triple (S,T,R), where R is a subset of S×T. For s∈S and t∈T, write sRt precisely when (s,t)∈R.

context: Binary relation identified with its graph subset

formulations.mathematical_scope_note: Only R is the mathematical relation object in this convention. Fixed S,T correspond to triples, but equality of typed triples is stronger than equality of bare graphs.
formulations.text: Given sets S and T, a binary relation from S to T may instead mean a subset R⊆S×T. The relation holds between s∈S and t∈T exactly when (s,t) belongs to R.

context: Set theory: Cartesian product of exactly two sets

formulations.mathematical_scope_note: Ordered pairs are foundational set-theoretic objects. This definition should not be conflated with scalar/vector cross products, nor with arbitrary indexed products.
formulations.text: For sets S and T, their Cartesian product is S×T = {(s,t) : s∈S and t∈T}, the set of all ordered pairs whose first entry belongs to S and whose second belongs to T.
